question: Whose administrative system later became the model for Emperor Akbar's consolidation of the Mughal Empire?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah Suri**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• **Sher Shah Suri**, the founder of the Sur Empire in North India, is renowned for his excellent administrative reforms that laid the foundation for efficient governance. 
• His administrative system became the model for **Emperor Akbar** in consolidating the Mughal Empire as it introduced systematic governance practices. 
• Sher Shah Suri is credited with standardizing **land revenue systems** by introducing a detailed land measurement system and fixing revenue rates based on productivity. This system was later adopted and refined by Akbar. 
• He established a network of **postal services**, improved infrastructure, and built roads like the famous **Grand Trunk Road**, all of which contributed to better connectivity and communication.
